findings.title: One schema conflates list rows and details
findings.why_it_matters: Future changes to either list_elements or get_element must expand the same broad schema with more optional fields or unions. That makes the advertised per-tool contracts accept impossible combinations and leaves maintainers unable to tell which fields each handler is responsible for without reading both implementations.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a small shared base for id/type, then define separate strict list-element and element-detail schemas (and discriminated association/lane variants where their shapes differ) and assign them to list_elements and get_element respectively.
evidence: src/server/tools.ts:316-351 defines outputQueryElement with nearly every field optional and models incoming/outgoing as number-or-array unions solely to cover two different endpoint representations.
src/server/tools.ts:455-459 reuses that schema for both list_elements.items and the complete get_element result.

src/server/handlers.ts:666-680 emits numeric incoming/outgoing counts for list rows, while src/server/handlers.ts:718-737 emits arrays plus properties for element details; association details take a third, smaller shape at lines 698-701.

findings.title: Exhaustive contract check is one serial scenario
findings.why_it_matters: A failure in any early lifecycle or mutation call aborts validation for every later tool, masking independent schema regressions and making unrelated contract changes share one large fixture and ordering dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract the advertised-schema validator/session fixture and split the assertions into a few independent scenarios such as query/export, mutation, file lifecycle, and collaboration outputs; retain a separate registry-parity assertion so every advertised name must still have an exercised scenario.
evidence: tests/e2e/server.test.ts:718-1002 contains all structured-output coverage in one approximately 280-line it block.
The scenario repeatedly creates, closes, reopens, renames, and deletes shared current-diagram state before later tool schemas can be checked (lines 784-983).
The completeness assertion against calledTools is only reached at lines 997-998, so any earlier failure prevents the test from identifying which other advertised tools have schema mismatches.

testing_gaps: The exhaustive success path does not exercise the distinct list/get query shapes for lanes and associations, so those polymorphic structured outputs are not contract-asserted through the real server.
Optional output branches are not exercised for an annotation without associationId, a black-box pool without processId, or delete_element's connection result.
No test deliberately injects a schema-invalid success payload to prove the shared output-validation boundary converts it into a protocol-compliant isError response without structuredContent.
